required-production-refinement: Scheduler inputs, phases, cursors, plans, and result stores use types that make invalid internal states unrepresentable
An empty input completes atomically with an empty plan, zero callbacks, and an empty committed observation
Schedule input is immutable after construction; execution owns or borrows a stable snapshot
PlanBuilder::build rejects exactly cyclic dependency graphs before execution
Resource admission rejects exactly tasks whose individual cost exceeds the budget, before execution
Rejected inputs publish no plan, worker result, commit, or callback
PlanBuilder uses stable task identifier as the unique tie breaker among ready tasks
PlanBuilder produces the unique deterministic first-fit plan for one immutable input
Every accepted task occurs exactly once in the flattened plan
Every batch stores tasks in strictly increasing stable-identifier order
No batch contains read/write or write/write conflicts
Effect conflict checks are symmetric and share one implementation kernel
The sum of costs in every batch is at most the configured budget
Every predecessor is assigned to a strictly earlier batch
Executor accepts a completion only for an uncompleted member of the current batch
Commit begins only after every task in the current batch has completed
Completed results are immutable and append-only until terminal cleanup
The accepted plan is immutable throughout execution
Observable commits are always a prefix of the flattened canonical plan
Each transition publishes at most one next canonical result
Every committed task has all predecessors in the earlier committed prefix
The first canonical non-success is published; when it is a failure execution terminates as failed without later commits
The first canonical non-success is published; when it is incomplete execution returns its structured reason without later commits
Cancellation request and acknowledgement occur at the exact configured canonical commit-count boundary before any later non-success
Completed means every task was committed exactly once and every outcome succeeded
